market_context: United States/general English; cooked kidney, black, white, pinto and navy beans
title: Types of beans and their nutritional differences

seo.title: Bean types compared: protein, fiber, iron and calories
seo.meta_description: Kidney, black, white, pinto and navy beans are similar in calories and protein when cooked, but fiber, iron, texture and size vary. Compare per 100 g.
seo.search_intent: Compare common bean types nutritionally and understand which differences actually matter.

excerpt: Common cooked beans differ more in color and texture than in basic macros: most references are around 125–145 calories and 8–10 g protein per 100 g. White beans can stand out for iron, while black, pinto and navy beans often provide substantial fiber.
content_html:
Black beans and white beans look very different, but their cooked macronutrient profiles overlap substantially. The useful differences are mostly fiber, selected minerals, seed size, skin and cooking texture.

Representative cooked values per 100 g

BeanCaloriesProteinFiberIron
Kidney~127~8.7 g~6.4 g~2.9 mg
Black~130–132~8.9 g~8.5 g~2.1 mg
White~135–140~9–10 g~6–10 g~3.5–3.7 mg
Pinto~140–145~9 g~8–9 g~2.1–2.3 mg
Navy~140~8 g~10 g~2.4 mg

These are representative USDA-style cooked references. Cultivar, hydration and cooking can move the exact values.

Protein is remarkably similar

The range of roughly 8–10 g protein/100 g spans only about 2 g. A 200 g serving therefore provides roughly 16–20 g protein across these types.

Fiber varies more

A navy-bean reference near 10 g fiber/100 g supplies about 20 g in a 200 g portion, while 200 g kidney beans at 6.4 g/100 g supply about 12.8 g. Both are still high-fiber foods.

White beans can stand out for iron

A white-bean reference around 3.7 mg iron/100 g provides roughly 1.6 mg more than a black-bean reference around 2.1 mg. Bean iron is nonheme iron, so vitamin C in the meal can improve absorption.

Culinary differences often matter more

Large white beans become creamy, black beans retain their distinctive color, pinto beans are versatile and navy beans work well in soups. Choosing for texture is often more useful than chasing a 5–10 calorie difference.

Bottom line

Kidney, black, white, pinto and navy beans all share the same nutritional strengths: plant protein, starch, fiber and minerals. Differences are real but modest enough that variety and preference can guide the choice.

faq.question: Which bean has the most protein?
faq.answer: Most cooked common beans cluster around 8–10 g/100 g, so differences are small and cultivar-dependent.

faq.question: Which beans have the most fiber?
faq.answer: Some navy-bean references approach 10 g/100 g cooked, compared with about 6.4 g for kidney beans.

faq.question: Which beans have more iron?
faq.answer: Some cooked white-bean references provide about 3.5–3.7 mg/100 g, compared with around 2.1 mg in black beans.
